fact: The Committee for Justice documented that Internal Security Agency personnel arrested Benghazi activist Aziz Al-Orfi over Facebook and TikTok posts on public affairs, and he says he was held five days on accusations of incitement.

A representative of Internet Society Libya said Article 39 (defamation) of the draft cybercrime law could be used to suppress activists and journalists, and proposed civil rather than criminal defamation.

Freedom House reports a localized internet shutdown in Tripoli in May 2025 amid antigovernment protests, lasting around 12 hours, with at least one provider reporting a total outage; the source does not name who ordered it.

Freedom House, citing Libya Crimes Watch, reports that Faisal Rajab al-Shikhi was detained in Benghazi in January 2025 by armed men of the Libyan Arab Armed Forces over a Facebook video critical of Khalifa Haftar, and his whereabouts were unknown at period end.

UNSMIL says it is concerned by continued reports of arbitrary arrest, detention and prosecution of journalists and critics in Libya, including use of cybercrime, counter-terrorism and penal provisions against expression; it names no person or date.
